newsitem.title: POLAND: No inflation threat from weaker Polish zloty - NBP.
newsitem.headline: No inflation threat from weaker Polish zloty - NBP.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland President Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said on Wednesday the bank was satisfied with the current level of the zloty and saw no inflationary pressure resulting from its recent weakening.

"We are now satisfied with it (the zloty level) and I believe It will not have an influence on inflation and it may also limit exporters' complaints", Gronkiewicz-Waltz told a news conference when asked about the zloty's future movement.

The zloty lost about two percent late in May following a pull-out of foreign investors from the region,triggered by the Czech crown slump, before rebounding to about 1.5 percent from parity, down from an earlier 2.5 percent level.

"We took advantage of the fact that the zloty weakened a bit (because of the crisis in Czech financial markets) but I think it is generally positive for the economy as a whole," Gronkiewicz-Waltz added.
The central bank has long voiced concern over Poland's widening trade and current account deficit and tailored its monetary policy to keep the deficit under control.
